name: KernelBench
intro: KernelBench 是一个评估语言模型能否为真实 PyTorch 机器学习工作负载生成正确且高效 GPU 内核的开放基准。论文合同包含 250 个仅用于评测的任务，并行分为 Level 1 单算子 100 题、Level 2 可融合算子序列 100 题和 Level 3 完整架构 50 题；每题仅提供 PyTorch 参考实现与输入生成器，不提供金标准内核。
build_method: 真实PyTorch工作负载整理, 并行三级任务分区, 参考实现与固定输入生成器打包
eval_feature: 仅评测, 无金标准内核, 五组随机输入正确性门控, L40S CUDA Event 计时
build_method_en: Real PyTorch Workload Curation, Three Parallel Task Partitions, Reference Model and Fixed Input-generator Packaging
eval_feature_en: Evaluation-only, No Gold Kernels, Five-random-input Correctness Gate, L40S CUDA-event Timing
intro_en: KernelBench is an open benchmark for evaluating whether language models can generate correct and efficient GPU kernels for real PyTorch machine-learning workloads. The paper contract contains 250 evaluation-only tasks in three parallel partitions: 100 Level 1 primitive operators, 100 Level 2 fusible operator sequences, and 50 Level 3 full architectures. Each task supplies only a PyTorch reference and input generators, not a gold optimized kernel.
metric_en: speedup_i = mean(T_Eager)/mean(T_New); fast_p = (1/N) sum_i 1[correct_i and speedup_i > p]

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2502.10517v1 and the ICML 2025 paper on OpenReview yeoN1iQT1x. The paper contract is exactly 250 evaluation-only tasks in three parallel partitions: Level 1 has 100 primitive operations, Level 2 has 100 multi-operator sequences with fusion opportunities, and Level 3 has 50 full ML architectures sourced from popular PyTorch repositories. The levels are independent partitions, not a serial transformation. Each task packages a torch.nn.Module Model plus get_inputs and get_init_inputs to fix shapes, dtypes, and initialization; no gold or optimized kernel is supplied. The paper reports no train/validation/test split, deduplication procedure, or contamination audit. A one-shot addition Model/ModelNew example and the task reference prompt greedy generation of ModelNew. Paper evaluation uses a bare-metal NVIDIA L40S Ada GPU with 48 GB memory and a 300 W power limit, Python 3.10, PyTorch 2.5.0+cu124, and CUDA 12.4. A candidate must compile and match the PyTorch Model on all five randomized inputs. Latency measurement uses three warm-ups and 100 CUDA-event trials for each implementation; speedup_i is mean PyTorch Eager latency divided by mean ModelNew latency. fast_p = (1/N) sum_i 1[correct_i and speedup_i > p], so fast_0 is the correctness fraction and fast_1 counts correct tasks faster than Eager. Artifact history is intentionally separated from the paper contract: Level 4 already existed in repository history before the paper, but is outside the paper's 250 tasks. Git 1f7b25b2c043907034c9cdaa1190c24400d921fe is only the closest identified paper-time candidate and is not an author-labeled release. Current Git revision 423217d9fda91e0c2d67e4a43bf62f96f6d104f1 has material task drift, while Hugging Face v0.1 revision ca1464e5d4723fd14f87b8e68306aaa1fe66b81b includes 20 Level 4 items even though the current loader accepts only Levels 1, 2, and 3.
drawio_evidence_note: Primary protocol evidence: arXiv:2502.10517v1 and ICML 2025 OpenReview yeoN1iQT1x. No repository commit is claimed as an author-designated paper release.
drawio_artifact_boundary_note: Paper scope is the 250 evaluation-only L1/L2/L3 tasks. Candidate Git 1f7b25b2c043907034c9cdaa1190c24400d921fe is untagged; current Git 423217d9fda91e0c2d67e4a43bf62f96f6d104f1 and HF v0.1 ca1464e5d4723fd14f87b8e68306aaa1fe66b81b are documented as drifted artifacts rather than paper-contract evidence.
